$comment: Dialect: JSON Schema draft-07. The dialect keyword is intentionally omitted so nothing has to be fetched over the network to validate this file; the consumer selects jsonschema.Draft7Validator explicitly.
title: SYNAPSE declared gate falsifications
description: Schema for infrastructure/quality/gate-mutations.yaml (AD-4; R1.2, R9.5, R12.3, R12.7). scripts/audit/gate_fault_injection.py validates the file, then for each operator copies the real tree to a temporary directory, applies the operator, and runs the gate as a SUBPROCESS. It never monkeypatches a gate's evaluator. A registered check absent from both `gates` and `reporting_tools` is UNDECLARED and is excluded from PASS-eligibility -- absence of a falsification is absence of proof (I-7), never a pass.

gates.description: Keyed by Check_Registry identifier (C<n>), matching the id the check is registered under in scripts/audit/verify_claims.py.

reporting_tools.description: Registered checks for which no falsifying mutation can be written. EXCLUDED from the PASS-eligible set. This is the honest label, not an exemption, and it never contributes a PASS.

operators.description: At least one mutation that MUST make this gate exit non-zero. A mutation the gate survives is a gate that does not gate.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the gate; reported in the fault-injection result.

target.description: Repo-relative path, or `path.py::Class.func` for replace_function_body. Interpreted inside the temporary tree copy, never against the working tree.

path.description: Location within the target document. Dotted/bracketed for set_yaml_path, JSONPath for set_json_path.

body.description: Source text: the new function body for replace_function_body, or the whole file for create_file.

expect_names.description: Substrings the gate's output MUST contain when it fails. `expect` is always "exits non-zero NAMING the mutated subject" -- a non-zero exit that names nothing does not satisfy the declaration.

reason.description: Why no falsifying mutation exists. Must describe the check's nature, not the cost of writing the mutation.

sweepBudget.description: AD-22 / R1.11: the sweep's cost budget as a pinned arithmetic claim. NOT in the root `required` set, deliberately: a declaration without it is still structurally valid, and the honest report of a missing budget belongs to the registered check (scripts/audit/sweep_budget_truth.py), not to a validation error that would make the whole declaration unusable. When present, that check asserts (baselines + operators) * per_subprocess_timeout_s + install_budget_s <= job_timeout_minutes * 60 over THIS file's own declared_gates and operator count, so the budget cannot silently stop fitting when another gate declares a mutation. The bounds are committed, not measured: a gate that cannot answer inside per_subprocess_timeout_s reports `indeterminate` naming the timeout, which is non-passing, never PASS-eligible, and therefore surfaces (I-7).

per_subprocess_timeout_s.description: Wall-clock bound on ONE gate subprocess, passed as --timeout under --sweep. Read from the declaration instead of scripts/audit/gate_fault_injection.py::DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S, so the bound the job runs under is the bound the inequality was checked against.

install_budget_s.description: Allowance for everything in the job that is not a gate subprocess (checkout, dependency install). An allowance, not an observation.

job_timeout_minutes.description: MUST equal `timeout-minutes` on the job that runs the sweep.

invariant.description: The obligation in one line, for a reader. The check re-derives it from the terms; it does not parse this string.

derivation.description: Where the counts in the inequality come from, recorded as pointers so a consumer reads its terms out of this file rather than hardcoding a count.

declared_gates.description: MUST equal the number of keys under `gates`, so a hand edit that disagrees is itself detectable.

enforced_by.description: The task that turns the declared-vs-registered shortfall into a gate. Until it lands, an undeclared check is reported as undeclared -- never as a pass.
